statements.venue: Press release introducing the Power for the People Act
statements.quote: Our Power for the People Act balances the need for data center development without pushing those costs onto consumers.
statements.context: Tonko introduced a bill making data centers, whose growth the release attributes to the rise of artificial intelligence models, pay for the grid expansion they require.
statements.reason: About the electricity costs of AI data centers, which the rubric places outside catastrophic risk.

slowdown.note: Co-sponsor of H.R. 10538, the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, which imposes a mandatory pause on advanced AI systems; a pause for safety reasons counts as yes here. Co-sponsorship, not a statement of his own.

pause.note: Co-sponsor of H.R. 10538; its pause on advanced AI lasts until the new Department of Artificial Intelligence is fully staffed and has issued rules (Section 8(b)), i.e. conditional on safety rules, which the rubric treats as mixed. No statement of his own on a pause found.

intl.note: H.R. 10538 Section 15(a) directs pursuit of 'international agreements and allied coordination to prevent the development of artificial superintelligence' but does not name China or pacing talks with China; no statement of his own found. Same reading as other co-sponsors' files.

rsi.note: Co-sponsor of H.R. 10538 (not his own statement). Its Section 9(a) bans systems with 'superintelligence precursor characteristics', defined in Section 3(6)(A) to include 'The capacity to automate or greatly accelerate the process of artificial intelligence research and development', and its mandatory pause covers training 'including through recursive self-improvement'. Same reading as other co-sponsors' files; a reviewer should confirm it.

record: Co-sponsor of H.R. 10538, the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act of 2026 (introduced 24 September 2026 by Rep. Casar), which bans artificial superintelligence and its precursor capabilities, imposes a mandatory pause on advanced AI until a new federal Department of Artificial Intelligence issues rules, and directs pursuit of international agreements. He is not among the original co-sponsors named in the introduced text, so he joined later; the date he joined was not found.
Introduced the Power for the People Act, requiring data centers rather than consumers to pay for the grid expansion their electricity demand causes.
grade_reason: No statement in his own words acknowledging catastrophic AI risk was found; his only AI remark found from 2026 is about data center electricity costs (D). His record does include co-sponsoring the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538) in 2026, a strong action on catastrophic risk, so a reviewer may want to grade higher on the record.
